transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Celestia - Head of Platform), Liam O'Sullivan (Celestia - SRE), Nora Kim (Celestia - Data Eng), Samir Desai (Celestia - PM)

--- Summary (auto):
Quick alignment on week-zero onramp tasks: staging cluster, networking, auth, sample data and pilot success criteria. Identified key owners and deadlines.

--- Topics: staging plan; VPC/peering; SSO & RBAC mapping; pilot metrics; telemetry/cost dashboards; next steps

--- Action items (captured live): see metadata and discussion section below

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll go quick — objective is week zero onramp, make sure we land staging and the test harness so you can start the pilot next week.
[00:12] Priya Rao: thanks Maya, excited to get started. we're aiming for a two week pilot with a handful of endpoints first. want to confirm the networking and data boundaries before we hand off infra tickets.
[00:25] Carlos Nguyen: yep, we'll cover that — I can walk through the redwood staging topology. this is Carlos (CSM) i'll be the day-to-day contact for access and onboarding tasks.
[00:36] Liam O'Sullivan: Liam here. on the SRE side we care about peering, NAT egress, and whether KMS/HSM calls leave our VPC — need confirmation on key management.
[00:49] Ethan Zhao: quick intro, ethan from solutions eng. i'll provision the staging cluster and set up preconfigured images and a small runtime pool to mimic your production qps. we'll also give you a runbook for smoke tests.
[01:02] Samir Desai: and Samir on product — i'll be owning success criteria, latency targets and what counts as pass/fail for the pilot.
[01:12] Maya Patel: great. high level items: 1) staging cluster spin up, 2) network peering and IP allowlist, 3) SSO & RBAC, 4) sample prompts/data, 5) telemetry and cost dashboards. we'll map owners now.
[01:28] Priya Rao: for SSO we are SAML via Okta, we need to map roles to our teams. also curious about audit logs retention — legal asked about 365-day retention.
[01:40] Carlos Nguyen: Redwood supports SAML SSO. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM; retention in hosted mode is 90 days by default but we can discuss an enterprise retention add-on or Private deployment for longer retention, if needed.
[01:58] Priya Rao: okay that's useful — for the pilot 90 days is fine, but we'll flag longer retention as a requirement for later.
[02:08] Liam O'Sullivan: about KMS — does Redwood's hosted offering require us to share keys, or can we bring our own?
[02:15] Ethan Zhao: you can bring your own keys via KMS integration in Private (or dedicated) options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS in supported regions — but I'll follow up with the exact KMS flow (there's a nuance around HSM-backed keys).
[02:33] Nora Kim: perfect. on the data side, we'll only be sending metadata and hashed identifiers in the first phase; full PII will be scrubbed upstream. want to validate that telemetry won't leak sample data.
[02:46] Carlos Nguyen: understood, we'll put guidance in the runbook — how telemetry samples are redacted and which fields are stored.
[02:52] Maya Patel: ok let's talk staging topology — Ethan, can you describe what you'll provision?
[02:59] Ethan Zhao: sure. I'll provision a small cluster with a 3-node gpu pool to replicate inference latency shape, a dev-only KV prefix cache, and a prefix cache hit policy enabled. we will also wire up continuous-batching to match typical burst patterns. note: in staging we won't enable aggressive quantization profiles unless you want us to test them.
[03:24] Priya Rao: what's the expected per-token cost delta between profiling with and without quantization?
[03:30] Ethan Zhao: rough ballpark — 20-40% cost reduction depending on model and sequence length; but quantization can increase latencies slightly for certain queries. we'll capture both in the cost dashboards during the pilot.
[03:44] Samir Desai: for success criteria i'd like to propose: 95th percentile latency under 300ms for the curated prompt set, and end-to-end errors under 1%. Thoughts?
[03:58] Maya Patel: reasonable target for your scale. we'll run the smoke tests to validate those numbers.
[04:07] Liam O'Sullivan: on peering — our network team requires the CIDR ranges and FQDNs that your staging nodes will egress to. can you share a diagram?
[04:17] Ethan Zhao: yes — I'll attach the staging architecture diagram and a list of IPs. we'll need your egress allowlist for callbacks and tracer endpoints.
[04:28] Priya Rao: related: do you support private endpoints inside our VPC so traffic never routes over the public internet?
[04:36] Carlos Nguyen: for private deployments yes; for hosted we do VPC peering or routed private connections depending on region and account tier. we'll send the options, but initial staging is usually peering.
[04:49] Nora Kim: testing data — we'll provide 3 datasets: short chat prompts, long-form descriptions, and a reranking set. we'll also share expected outputs for quality checks.
[04:58] Ethan Zhao: excellent. please send them to the shared drive; I'll load them into the test harness and create perf+quality dashboards.
[05:10] Maya Patel: security questions — Priya raised audit logs and KMS. any other compliance asks?
[05:17] Priya Rao: SOC2 and ISO are on the list; we also need to know whether you have penetration test reports and if there's an external contact if our security team has follow-ups.
[05:27] Carlos Nguyen: we will share our SOC2 report and pen-test summary under NDA. i'll drop contact details for our security lead in the follow-up email.
[05:36] Samir Desai: curious about rollout strategy post-pilot — can we do canary with percentage traffic split?
[05:44] Ethan Zhao: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B testing by route. you can pin model versions and route by policy; we can demo the traffic split in the deep-dive.
[05:55] Priya Rao: can you explain cost monitoring? we need token-level breakdowns per route and per model.
[06:03] Carlos Nguyen: Redwood Console exposes token by route, by model, and we can produce daily cost exports. for the pilot we'll set up a dashboard and alerting for cost spikes.
[06:14] Liam O'Sullivan: is there an option to throttle at the router level to prevent runaway costs from a bad prompt?
[06:20] Ethan Zhao: yes, there are rate limits and quotas you can enforce at token and request level; also a circuit-breaker policy if error rates spike.
[06:30] Maya Patel: okay let's set timing: Ethan will provision by Monday 3/22, Carlos sends console access by 3/18, Celestia confirms peering by 3/19, and Nora shares datasets by 3/20. after that we'll run the smoke suite and meet for an SE deep-dive on 3/24.
[06:50] Priya Rao: that timeline works. one more thing — do you have guidance for prompt engineering to avoid hallucination in our reranker tests?
[06:58] Ethan Zhao: yes, we'll include prompt templates, temperature/penalty suggestions, and recommended evals. also suggest using a reranker model for safety checks before surface to users.
[07:12] Samir Desai: will the reranker be hosted as a separate model version or inline?
[07:17] Ethan Zhao: typically separate route — easier to monitor and scale independently. we can show an example config.
[07:26] Lara (automatic note): [background noise] i may have misheard last bit, \"r-a-n-k-er\" typed as reranker in the transcript.
[07:33] Carlos Nguyen: noted — we'll share configuration examples in the repo.
[07:39] Priya Rao: about support SLAs during the pilot — what's the expected response time for Sev1 vs Sev2?
[07:45] Carlos Nguyen: for pilot customers we offer business-hours support with target 4-hour response for Sev1; enterprise support tiers have faster SLAs. We'll outline options in the follow-up.
[07:57] Liam O'Sullivan: any limits on model variants we can test in staging?
[08:03] Ethan Zhao: no hard limit for staging; we'll provision a couple of model variants and you can toggle. heavy parallel variants may require dedicated pool sizing.
[08:14] Nora Kim: how does KV caching behave across restarts? we need cache warming guidance to avoid cold-start spikes.
[08:21] Ethan Zhao: KV cache is persisted in our runtime between restarts for dedicated and private setups; in hosted staging it persists as long as the instance is live. we'll include cache warmup scripts and guidelines.
[08:35] Priya Rao: good to know. Samir — do you have any operational acceptance criteria for rollout?
[08:40] Samir Desai: yes, we'll define an Ops checklist: monitoring alerts, error thresholds, cost guardrails, and a rollback plan. if all green then we scale to small % production traffic after pilot.
[08:52] Maya Patel: excellent. any blockers from Celestia's side?
[08:55] Priya Rao: internal approval for peering may take 48 hours, but otherwise no blockers. we'll prioritize the IP ranges.
[09:04] Carlos Nguyen: i'll follow up with a single email containing: staging access, runbook draft, SOC2/pen-test link (NDA), and the proposed smoke test plan.
[09:13] Ethan Zhao: i'll attach the staging diagram and initial manifests.
[09:18] Priya Rao: thanks — look forward to the deep-dive on 3/24.
[09:22] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, we'll close with a quick recap and owners.
[09:27] Carlos Nguyen: recap: Ethan — staging & manifests by 3/22; Carlos — console access & security docs by 3/18; Celestia (Priya/Nora/Liam) — peering confirmation by 3/19 and datasets by 3/20; deep-dive 3/24.
[09:45] Priya Rao: confirmed.
[09:48] Samir Desai: thanks all.
[09:50] Maya Patel: meeting adjourned.

--- End of transcript
